Fix Linear ticket COR-2207 in the entire-brain repo (you are in an isolated worktree of it). Follow the repo's CLAUDE.md / .entire/agent-guide.md workflow (Brain brief preflight etc.).

## Ticket: brain connect placement error embeds raw host-CLI noise and a dangling clause (Low)

Repro: `entire brain connect` on a repo with no stored coordinates and no hosted placement (repo not visible from the login).

Observed:
```
connect: resolve hosted placement (`entire repo view --json`): entire [repo view --json]: exit status 1: Using context 'us.auth.entire.io'.
no repo matching "sandbox-audit/brain-sbx" visible from your login (GitHub repos you could onboard: `entire repo mirror list --available`)
; pass --repo-id and --api-url explicitly
```
Problems: debug framing on the human surface (the backtick command, the argv echo `entire [repo view --json]: exit status 1:`, the host CLI's "Using context …" banner); the embedded stderr's trailing newline leaves `; pass --repo-id and --api-url explicitly` dangling on a line starting with `;`.

Expected shape:
```
connect: no repo matching "sandbox-audit/brain-sbx" is visible from your login.
See onboardable repos: entire repo mirror list --available
Or pass --repo-id and --api-url explicitly.
```
The useful content (no matching repo, mirror-list hint, explicit-flags fallback) already exists — fix the framing.

## Approach notes
- Grep `resolve hosted placement` to find the wrapping site (likely a connect-related file in internal/cli/). The repo has a `providerdetail.Flatten` helper used elsewhere to summarize sub-CLI stderr — check whether reusing it (or extracting the meaningful stderr line) fits before writing new parsing.
- Strip host-CLI banners like `Using context '…'.` and the argv echo from the human surface; keep the host CLI's meaningful message. Fix the dangling `;` by composing the fallback hint as its own sentence/line.
- Note COR-2202 recently reworked connect's sync reporting — read the recent git history of the connect files first (`git log --oneline -10 -- <file>`) and respect its decisions.
- Keep the fix scoped to connect's placement-resolution error path; avoid touching internal/factsync, add.go, distill, privacy files (parallel agents own those).
- Update or add a focused test pinning the new message.

## Workflow requirements
1. `git fetch origin main` and create your branch from `origin/main`: `git checkout -b cor-2207-connect-placement-error origin/main`.
2. Minimal change, repo idiom (comments explain WHY only).
3. Run `gofmt -l -s` on changed files (must be empty) and focused tests plus one full `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1` (takes ~7 min; must pass).
4. Commit with explicit file names (never `git add -A`). End the commit message with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
5. Push the branch (a first push may be transiently rejected — retry once). Create the PR: `gh pr create --base main` with a cold-reader body (Why / What changed / Validation), ending with:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
6. Do NOT touch Linear; the parent session handles it.

Report back: PR URL, 3-5 bullets on what changed, the exact new error output, validation run, any risks.

a relationship question.

committed-tree results as analysis of edits they do not contain.

Ask per-symbol commands before bulk streams. Never dump unfiltered whole-repo

inspection. State unresolved coverage limits in the answer.

Both sets of mandatory rules apply.
Brain answers recorded-context and historical questions; Graph answers structural
questions and entity-level revision comparisons.

They NEVER replace required neighbors or impact analysis.
Graph results NEVER replace required retrieval of prior decisions or attempts.

location; it NEVER exempts relationship questions from Graph or historical
questions from Brain. Small edits, follow-ups, read-only reconnaissance, specs,

an answered question in source is not verification.

a reproduction, or the most relevant build. If execution is unavailable, disclose
that limit and perform a bounded source check. Prefer precise queries and line ranges,
but never trade resolution for fewer turns.

Current source and executed tests establish present behavior. Historical memory

1	// Package providerdetail renders the one failure a first run is most likely to
2	// hit: the entire-graph provider is not installed, so every component that
3	// shells out to `entire graph ...` fails with the host CLI's full usage dump.
4	//
5	// It lives in its own package because TWO components fail from that single
6	// cause -- the semantic index (internal/cli) and the entity index
7	// (internal/entityindex) -- and for a long while only one of them had been
8	// taught to summarise it. The semantic index reported one readable line naming
9	// the install step; the entity index embedded 60 lines of `entire --help` and a
10	// "Did you mean this? grant" that implied the reader had mistyped a command
11	// they never typed. Two different messages for one cause is the defect, and a
12	// private copy in each package is how it comes back, so the summary rule, the
13	// detection markers and the remedy sentence have exactly one home here.
14	package providerdetail
15	
16	import (
17		"fmt"
18		"strings"
19	)
20	
21	const (
22		// BrainBinaryName is this program's own name: what a reader who runs it
23		// directly types.
24		BrainBinaryName = "entire-brain"
25		// EntireBinaryName is the host CLI that dispatches the brain as an external
26		// command, and brainPluginVerb is the verb it dispatches on.
27		EntireBinaryName = "entire"
28		brainPluginVerb  = "brain"
29		// PluginCommand is the plugin spelling: what the reader types when they
30		// reach this binary through the Entire CLI.
31		PluginCommand = EntireBinaryName + " " + brainPluginVerb
32	
33		// envCLIVersion is set by the Entire CLI's plugin dispatcher on every
34		// plugin launch, and is the only signal that distinguishes the two
35		// spellings. See SetupCommand.
36		envCLIVersion = "ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION"
37	
38		// InstallGraphCommand is the one runnable way to get the provider: `graph`
39		// is in the Entire CLI's official plugin index (`entire plugin search
40		// graph`), so this works for a reader who has only the CLI.
41		InstallGraphCommand = EntireBinaryName + " plugin install graph"
42	
43		// MaxSummary caps a summarised detail so one failure cannot own the
44		// terminal even when the subprocess writes a single enormous line.
45		MaxSummary = 200
46	)
47	
48	// EnvLookup is os.LookupEnv, taken as an argument so the resolution is testable
49	// without mutating the process environment.
50	type EnvLookup func(string) (string, bool)
51	
52	// Summary reduces a subprocess failure to one printable line.
53	//
54	// A CLI answers an unknown command by dumping its ENTIRE usage text -- sixty
55	// lines of command groups and flags -- to stderr, and that text arrives here as
56	// the error detail. Printed whole it buries the one sentence that matters
57	// inside setup's failure line, its summary block, `status` and `doctor` alike.
58	// The line the CLI marks with "Error:" is that sentence; the first line is the
59	// fallback for tools that do not mark one.
60	//
61	// Detection still runs against the FULL detail, so shortening what is shown
62	// never changes what is recognised.
63	func Summary(detail string) string {
64		detail = strings.TrimSpace(detail)
65		if detail == "" {
66			return ""
67		}
68		lines := strings.Split(detail, "\n")
69		summary := strings.TrimSpace(lines[0])
70		for _, line := range lines {
71			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
72			if after, ok := strings.CutPrefix(line, "Error:"); ok {
73				summary = strings.TrimSpace(after)
74				break
75			}
76		}
77		summary = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(summary), "Usage:")
78		summary = strings.TrimSpace(summary)
79		if runes := []rune(summary); len(runes) > MaxSummary {
80			summary = strings.TrimSpace(string(runes[:MaxSummary])) + "..."
81		}
82		return summary
83	}
84	
85	// Flatten is the last net before a detail reaches a terminal: it guarantees the
86	// invariant every one-line report depends on, that a reported detail occupies
87	// ONE line, WITHOUT shortening a detail that a producer already summarised.
88	//
89	// A producer that already composed a single line -- summary plus the remedy
90	// sentence, which is deliberately longer than MaxSummary -- passes through
91	// untouched. Only a detail that still carries a newline, i.e. one nobody
92	// summarised, is reduced. That asymmetry is the point: the net exists for the
93	// component nobody has fixed yet, not to truncate the ones already correct.
94	func Flatten(detail string) string {
95		if !strings.ContainsAny(detail, "\n\r") {
96			return strings.TrimSpace(detail)
97		}
98		return Summary(detail)
99	}
100	
101	// Missing recognises the provider-absent shape of a failure -- the host CLI
102	// rejecting an unknown `graph` command, or the binary not being on PATH at all
103	// -- as opposed to a provider that ran and reported something. Matching on text
104	// is unavoidable here: the failure is another process's exit status plus its
105	// stderr, and there is no typed error to switch on across a process boundary.
106	func Missing(detail string) bool {
107		text := strings.ToLower(detail)
108		if text == "" {
109			return false
110		}
111		for _, marker := range []string{
112			`unknown command "graph"`,
113			"unknown command 'graph'",
114			"unknown command graph",
115			"executable file not found",
116			"no such file or directory",
117			"command not found",
118			// Newer host CLIs have a `graph` dispatcher that reports the absent
119			// plugin by name instead of rejecting an unknown command. Added on
120			// main while this package was being extracted; folding the two
121			// implementations together must not drop it.
122			"plugin is not installed",
123		} {
124			if strings.Contains(text, marker) {
125				return true
126			}
127		}
128		return false
129	}
130	
131	// SetupCommand answers the question every printed command depends on: WHICH of
132	// the two spellings of this program did the reader actually type?
133	//
134	// The brain ships as a kubectl-style external command of the Entire CLI. A
135	// reader who types `entire brain setup` never types the binary's own name, and
136	// on a managed install (`entire plugin install`) they cannot: the binary lives
137	// in <xdg_data>/entire/plugins/bin, a directory the Entire CLI prepends to PATH
138	// inside its OWN process and nowhere else. Printing `entire-brain status` to
139	// that reader hands them a command their shell cannot resolve.
140	//
141	// THE SIGNAL, and it is the host's, not ours: the Entire CLI's plugin
142	// dispatcher sets ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION in the child's environment unconditionally
143	// on every plugin launch. It is the only unconditional one -- ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT
144	// is set only inside a worktree, and ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR is dropped when the
145	// data dir cannot be resolved. os.Args[0] is NOT a signal: the dispatcher execs
146	// the resolved binary path, so argv[0] is the same absolute path a standalone
147	// run of that file would carry.
148	//
149	// The fallback is the standalone name, which is the honest answer when nothing
150	// says otherwise: a reader with no ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION reached this binary
151	// directly, and may not have the Entire CLI at all.
152	func SetupCommand(lookup EnvLookup) string {
153		if lookup == nil {
154			return BrainBinaryName
155		}
156		// A marker present but EMPTY does not count: exporting NAME= to clear it is
157		// how a reader turns a signal off.
158		if value, ok := lookup(envCLIVersion); ok && strings.TrimSpace(value) != "" {
159			return PluginCommand
160		}
161		return BrainBinaryName
162	}
163	
164	// MissingRemedy is the sentence both the semantic index and the entity index
165	// append when Missing says the provider simply is not installed: what is
166	// missing, how the reader can tell, the command that fixes it, and the command
167	// to run afterwards. One home, so the two components cannot disagree about the
168	// remedy for the same cause.
169	//
170	// The command is InstallGraphCommand, NOT the `scripts/install.sh` form this
171	// sentence used to carry. That form is not runnable for the reader who hits
172	// this: it presupposes an entire-brain source checkout, which someone who
173	// installed the brain as a plugin does not have. `graph` is in the official
174	// plugin index, so one command installs it from anywhere.
175	// MissingSuffix is the clause to append to message: the remedy when the
176	// provider is missing, and nothing when message already carries it.
177	//
178	// A host CLI whose own stderr names `entire plugin install graph` made both
179	// the semantic index and the entity index print the install sentence twice,
180	// because each decided for itself and neither looked at what the host had
181	// already said. Deciding here is the same rule as MissingRemedy: one home,
182	// so the two components cannot disagree -- including about when NOT to speak.
183	//
184	// Note WHICH two strings this reads, because the obvious version is wrong.
185	// Whether the provider is missing is decided on the FULL detail, since the
186	// marker is often below the host's usage text. Whether the remedy would be a
187	// REPEAT is decided on the message being built, which is the summary -- and
188	// the summary is exactly what cuts the host's own remedy line. Deduping
189	// against the detail therefore suppresses a sentence the reader never
190	// received, and the first version of this did that: the output lost the
191	// install command entirely for the one host that had tried to be helpful.
192	func MissingSuffix(message, detail, graphBinary string, lookup EnvLookup) string {
193		if !Missing(detail) || strings.Contains(message, InstallGraphCommand) {
194			return ""
195		}
196		return "; " + MissingRemedy(graphBinary, lookup)
197	}
198	
199	func MissingRemedy(graphBinary string, lookup EnvLookup) string {
200		binary := strings.TrimSpace(graphBinary)
201		if binary == "" {
202			binary = EntireBinaryName
203		}
204		return fmt.Sprintf(
205			"the entire-graph semantic provider is not installed (%s has no `graph` command)"+
206				" -- install it with `%s`, then re-run `%s setup`",
207			binary, InstallGraphCommand, SetupCommand(lookup))
208	}
